title: The ghost who never checked out: The mystery of Room 311

content:
CHATTANOOGA — Behind the elegant doors of Chattanooga’s historic Read House Hotel is a room with a reputation that refuses to check out.

Room 311 blends nearly 150 years of history with a chilling legend, where stories of a mysterious guest, strange encounters and a ghostly presence continue to keep visitors guessing.

The History

The Read House Hotel has stood in downtown Chattanooga since 1872, becoming one of the city’s most recognizable landmarks through decades of Chattanooga history.

The hotel, built during reconstruction after the Civil War, survived many changes before being restored to its 1920s appearance in 2018.

Among its many rooms, Room 311 became one of the most talked-about spaces because of the legends and stories surrounding its past.

The room was restored with vintage furnishings, a clawfoot tub and a physical key to reflect the style of the 1920s.

A legend is born

According to local lore, Room 311 is haunted by the spirit of Annalisa Netherly, a former guest who allegedly died there in 1927.

The legend claims Netherly was killed in the bathroom by a jealous lover.

Over the years, guests have shared stories of unexplained noises, flickering lights, running water and shadowy figures inside the historic room.

Some visitors claim they have felt a presence in the room, while others say they have seen a figure believed to be Netherly.

Stay is you dare

The legend has helped make Room 311 become one of Chattanooga’s most famous local ghost folklore.

Today, visitors can experience the mystery themselves by requesting a tour or booking a stay in Room 311 through The Read House.

The room’s historic design gives guests a glimpse into the hotel’s past while adding to the atmosphere behind its haunted reputation.

For those looking for a spooky Chattanooga experience, Room 311 offers a mix of history, mystery and stories that have lasted for nearly a century.
